Information needed: Age in years
English question or message (reference): How old are you, in years?
Wording notes: Adult demo: 18 years and above. No separate detail follow-up.

Information needed: Reported sex
English question or message (reference): What sex do you report?
Wording notes: Use the definition and wording agreed with the nurse.

Information needed: Main reason for seeking help
English question or message (reference): What is your main concern?
English follow-up (reference): What specific problem brought you here?
Wording notes: Ask for the specific concern only when the answer is vague.

Information needed: What the person feels and relevant symptom details
English question or message (reference): What does it feel like?
English follow-up (reference): Where is it, and what does it feel like?
Wording notes: Ask for missing location or description only when needed.

Information needed: Other symptoms the person reports
English question or message (reference): Any other symptoms?
Wording notes: Keep an explicit none separate from unknown.

Information needed: Existing known medical conditions
English question or message (reference): Any known medical conditions?
English follow-up (reference): Which conditions have you been told you have?
Wording notes: Ask for reported conditions. Do not infer a diagnosis.

Information needed: Known allergies
English question or message (reference): Any known allergies?
Wording notes: Ask what the person is allergic to only when clarification is needed.

Information needed: Medicines taken regularly
English question or message (reference): Do you take any regular medications?
English follow-up (reference): What are the names of your regular medications?
Wording notes: Ask for names if the reply only confirms medicine use. Do not request doses.

Information needed: When the symptoms started
English question or message (reference): When did this start?
English follow-up (reference): Do you know when it started?
Wording notes: Do not ask again if the timing is already clear.

Information needed: How long symptoms have lasted
English question or message (reference): How long has it been going on?
English follow-up (reference): About how many minutes, hours or days?
Wording notes: A clear timing answer may already cover onset and duration.

Information needed: Reported symptom severity or effect on activities
English question or message (reference): How strong is it, or how does it affect what you can do?
English follow-up (reference): How does it affect what you can do?
Wording notes: Do not invent a pain score or require one for every symptom.

Information needed: Whether symptoms are worsening, improving, or unchanged
English question or message (reference): Is it getting worse, improving, or staying the same?
Wording notes: Preserve all three possibilities in the question.

Information needed: Tests already performed: names or context only
English question or message (reference): Any tests already done? Names only.
English follow-up (reference): What tests were done? Names only.
Wording notes: Do not request test results or measured values.

Information needed: Tests already requested by a clinician: names or context only
English question or message (reference): Any tests requested by a clinician? Names only.
English follow-up (reference): What tests did the clinician request? Names only.
Wording notes: Do not suggest new tests or request test results.

Information needed: Existing medical devices or catheters being used
English question or message (reference): Do you use any medical device or catheter?
English follow-up (reference): What device or catheter do you use?
Wording notes: Ask for the name or type when needed.

Information needed: Greeting, stub number, fictional-demo context, and permission to skip unknowns
English question or message (reference): Hi! Your stub is :stub. Tell me about the fictional case in your own words. I’ll pick up the details you share and ask only for what’s still missing. You can skip anything you don’t know.
Wording notes: Keep :stub exactly as written.

Information needed: Invite the person to explain their main concern
English question or message (reference): What brings you in today? Tell me what you’re feeling.
Wording notes: Keep the question open and conversational.

Information needed: Ask the person to review collected details before submitting
English question or message (reference): Thanks, that’s enough to review. I’ve put your answers together below. Check or correct anything before submitting.
Wording notes: Refer to the review section below the conversation.

Information needed: Explain that the reply could not be processed and can be sent again
English question or message (reference): I couldn’t read that reply just now. Your draft is still here. Please send it again, or skip these details for now.
Wording notes: Keep the options to retry or skip.

Information needed: Record that the person reviewed and corrected collected details
English question or message (reference): I reviewed and corrected the collected details before submitting.
Wording notes: This message is written from the person's perspective.

Information needed: Unknown or information not provided
English question or message (reference): Unknown / not supplied
Wording notes: Do not translate this as none or no symptoms.

Information needed: No additional details were provided
English question or message (reference): No further details supplied
Wording notes: This does not mean the original symptom or condition is absent.

Information needed: Button for unknown information or skipping a question
English question or message (reference): I don’t know / skip
Wording notes: Use a short button label.

Information needed: Button for continuing without more detail
English question or message (reference): Continue without more details
Wording notes: Use a short button label.
